Due dates

Half due by April 30 and half by October 31 (statewide schedule; the Minnehaha Treasurer pages opened did not state dates). Not delinquent if half paid before May 1 and the remainder before Nov 1.. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Per the SD DOR 2026 appeal guide: assessment notices mailed by March 1; written appeal to the clerk of the local board of equalization by March 12 (2026 dates); local board meets March 16-20 and must give written decision by March 27; then written appeal to the county auditor by April 7 for the county board of equalization (meets April 14-May 5; decision notice by May 8); then Office of Hearing Examiners by May 15 or circuit court within 30 days of notice. Sioux Falls by the numbers

Which county bills my Sioux Falls property tax?

Most Sioux Falls parcels are billed by Minnehaha County, and the part of the city that extends into Lincoln County is billed by the Lincoln County Treasurer. Sioux Falls is the county seat of Minnehaha County and the largest city in South Dakota, with 213,748 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate.

The tax notice names the county, so check it before you call anyone. The two treasurer offices are separate.

OfficePhoneUsed for
Minnehaha County Treasurer(605) 367-4211Bills, payments, delinquent tax questions
Minnehaha County Equalization(605) 367-4228Owner-occupancy and assessment questions
Minnehaha County Auditor(605) 367-4220Levies and budgets
Lincoln County Treasurer(605) 764-5701Parcels in the Lincoln County part of the city

How does the tax bill get from an assessment to a payment?

Three offices split the work. The Director of Equalization appraises and assesses property, the Auditor calculates taxes from the budgets set by elected boards, and the Treasurer bills and collects.

The legal assessment date is November 1 of each year, and the condition of the property that day sets the next year's assessment. Residential land is generally valued by front feet. Building value depends on quality, size, design, condition and extras, and the structure is then depreciated. General maintenance does not raise an assessment, but a major addition can.

A mill is one-tenth of a penny, or $1 for each $1,000 of assessed value, according to Pennington County's explanation of the state system. Each taxing body, such as the city, the county and the school district, sets its own levy. Records are public, and reviewing your own parcel is free at the Minnehaha Equalization office.

What are the payment dates, penalties and ways to pay?

Minnehaha County taxes are due January 1, with the first half accepted without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31. They become delinquent on May 1 and November 1, and late payments carry a 10 percent annual penalty, about 0.83333 percent a month.

  • If April 30 or October 31 falls on a weekend or holiday, payment is due by 4:45 p.m. on the last working day.
  • Drop-box and online payments are accepted until midnight.
  • Credit cards carry a 2.35 percent convenience fee.
  • Online electronic check payments take 7 to 10 business days to post to the account.
  • Paper checks must be pre-printed, in-state checks with the name and address embossed in the upper left corner.
  • The county no longer takes early payments, and there is no discount for paying early.

Delinquent taxpayers cannot pay online and need to call the Treasurer's Office. Mail goes to 415 N. Dakota Ave., Sioux Falls, SD 57104. Include the stub, and a stamped self-addressed envelope if you want a receipt.

Why does owner-occupied status change a Sioux Falls tax bill?

South Dakota taxes owner-occupied homes at a lower rate than other property, and the classification has to be claimed. Under SDCL 10-13-40, the owner files a certificate with the county director of equalization stating that the owner owns and lives in the dwelling as the principal residence on the assessment date.

  • The certificate is due by March 15.
  • The classification applies to only one dwelling in the state.
  • Once granted, it stays until ownership transfers or the use changes.
  • A new owner can meet the requirement by filing the certificate of value at transfer, or by applying between November 1 and March 15.
  • A dispute over the classification goes to the county board of equalization.

The classification matters when a house sells. If a buyer moves in after November 1, they apply for the following year. Ask your title company how the current year's bill will be split.

What is changing in South Dakota property taxes after 2025?

Recent state laws cap growth in owner-occupied valuations and lower the school levy. The Department of Revenue lists three changes that affect Sioux Falls homeowners.

  • SB 216 (2025) caps annual increases in owner-occupied valuation at 3 percent per county and limits local government property tax budget growth to 3 percent. It applies to 2026 assessment notices and taxes paid in 2027, and it is temporary for five years.
  • SB 245 (2026) uses a 0.3 percent sales tax increase to fund schools and lower the owner-occupied school levy, with a one-time payment so all homeowners see a lower school levy on their 2027 bill.
  • SB 96 (2026) lets counties add a local sales tax of up to 0.5 percent, subject to a possible public vote, with the revenue used for a county credit on owner-occupied property.

The Sioux Falls School District reports that its mil rate would drop from $7.13 in 2026 to $5.36 in 2027, which it describes as a 23 percent cut on a typical home. The district notes that the legal notice is titled Notice of Tax Increase, a label it calls misleading. Minnehaha County's fiscal 2027 budget is $144,605,790, and property taxes make up 58 percent of county revenue. The county levy total is 2.940, up 0.24 percent from fiscal 2026.

What tax relief is available for Sioux Falls homeowners?

Several programs reduce or defer tax for owner-occupants who qualify, and most have an April 1 deadline. The county treasurer handles the applications.

  • Assessment Freeze for seniors and disabled owners: age 65 or older or legally disabled, with income limits, filed by April 1.
  • Homestead Exemption: defers payment until the property is sold, available at age 70 under SDCL 43-31-1, filed by April 1.
  • Disabled Veteran exemption: for owner-occupied homes of veterans rated permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition, filed by November 1 with the Director of Equalization.

The City of Sioux Falls also refunds the municipal part of the tax for low-income elderly or disabled owner-occupants who are approved for the state freeze. The refund is up to $500, paid the year after approval, and residents do not apply to the city. The city's refund page has two different home-value thresholds, so verify the current limit with the city or county. Lincoln County residents file with the Lincoln County treasurer.

What happens if a Sioux Falls property tax goes unpaid?

Unpaid property tax in South Dakota becomes a lien, and after enough time the county can take the property by tax deed. The statutes set the steps.

  1. Half of the tax is delinquent on May 1 and the other half on November 1 if unpaid by October 31 (SDCL 10-21-23).
  2. Interest runs monthly from each delinquency date, at five-sixths of one percent per month.
  3. The treasurer may offer tax certificates at a public sale on the third Monday of December (SDCL 10-23-7). Pennington County notes that this happens only when the commissioners authorize it.
  4. A tax deed proceeding can start three years after the certificate sale and must finish within six years (SDCL 10-25-1).
  5. The holder serves notice of intention to take a tax deed, and the right to redeem ends 60 days after the affidavit of service is filed.

Redemption stays open until a deed is issued. Property taxes are a first-priority lien, and Pennington County says neither the Treasurer nor the commissioners can forgive interest or penalties. Minnehaha practice may differ in details, so call (605) 367-4211 for a payoff figure.

How are property taxes handled when you sell a Sioux Falls house?

The unpaid tax is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so a back-tax balance normally does not stop a sale. South Dakota's recording process also asks for a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56) with every deed, listing the price and the parties. The register of deeds cannot accept a deed without it.

The transfer fee is imposed under SDCL 43-4-21, and Minnehaha County's schedule lists $1.00 per thousand of value, with a $30.00 recording fee for the deed. If you used the Homestead Exemption, the deferred taxes and interest are paid out of the sale.

More questions about Sioux Falls, SD Property Tax Guide

When are Sioux Falls property taxes due?

Minnehaha County taxes are due January 1, with the first half accepted through April 30 and the second half through October 31. They become delinquent on May 1 and November 1.

What is the penalty for paying Sioux Falls property tax late?

Minnehaha County says late payments incur a 10 percent annual penalty, about 0.83333 percent per month.

How do I get the owner-occupied rate on my Sioux Falls home?

File a certificate with the county director of equalization by March 15, stating you own and live in the home on the assessment date. A new owner files after the transfer, between November 1 and March 15.

Can I pay Minnehaha County property tax online?

Yes, by electronic check or Discover, Visa or Mastercard through the county's payment portal. Cards carry a 2.35 percent fee, and online payments take 7 to 10 business days to post. Delinquent accounts cannot be paid online.

Is my Sioux Falls house in Minnehaha or Lincoln County?

Most of the city is in Minnehaha County, and a smaller area is in Lincoln County. Your tax notice shows the county.

What is the Sioux Falls property tax refund?

The city refunds the municipal portion of tax, up to $500, for low-income elderly or disabled owner-occupants approved for the state assessment freeze. Residents apply through the county treasurer by April 1.

Can I sell my Sioux Falls house if taxes are delinquent?

Yes. The unpaid tax and interest are paid from the proceeds at closing. Call the Treasurer's Office for the payoff amount.
